notes: Interest rate cards show one rate instead of Multiple rates: the average weighted by how much is in each, or the payout yield when no rate is entered
Upcoming commitments are tidier: Due now first, then the next 30 days, then what looks regular, with amounts lined up on the right
Payouts as they come: for investments with no schedule, such as dairy cattle paying each lactation, record each payout when it arrives
Units that pay on their own, such as 28 cows: set the expected amount per cow and how often, see the monthly average, and record how many paid each time
The card's button says Payout, or Interest for deposits and bonds
Investments can have a maturity date: payouts stop after it, and Home reminds you a month before to record the principal coming back
A payout can rise each year by a percentage, such as rent going up 5% a year
Editing a holding can move it between Investments, PF, PPF and NPS, and change how a custom type grows
On desktop, Future and Insights are tabs of their own in the top bar; phones keep Plan
Recent activity shows whose account it is instead of the account number, and how far each value update moved
Scheduled contributions read as Monthly contribution, and desktop tabs are roomier
Faster to open: the first download is smaller, and setup, the lock screen and the Features and Privacy pages load only when needed
